clue.text: Drink emptied after drink round joint, an extended skinful?

indicators.note: after places the emptied drink at the end of the answer
round means the soft drink is placed around the joint

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
the hip is a joint of the body

indicators.note: emptied means the word loses its inside, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A drinker downs one drink after another round a pub joint and ends up with quite a skinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinful' suggests a heavy drinking session, but here it is a long casing filled with meat; 'emptied' leaves the tea drink as its outer pair, and 'round' wraps the cola around the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, playfully described as a stretched-out casing stuffed full.

clue.text: Richard the First of France to steal short uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the whole string is read from bottom to top
the first of a word is its opening letter
short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: to filch is to steal

explanation.surface: Richard I of France makes off with something in a brief rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the First of' takes F from France; 'short' cuts FILCH to FILC; 'uprising' turns FFILC around. Cliff Richard is a British pop singer, so Richard is the definition by the first-name trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard is a famous British singer, so his first name is clued by his surname.

clue.text: 1p right in coin to stamp

parts.note: the digit one looks like the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the coin word

parts.note: to mint is to coin money
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A one-penny piece gets a proper stamping at the mint.
explanation.walkthrough: '1p' reads as a single coin, but the 1 gives I at the front and the p goes with R inside MINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprint is to stamp a mark or design onto a surface.

clue.text: Politician topless, then vote for the horny beast!

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
a cross, X, marks a vote for a candidate on a ballot

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to back a beast, after a politician has stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes T from TORY. TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large antelope with long straight horns.

clue.text: Pain of unlimited distinction

indicators.note: unlimited means the word loses its boundaries, its first and last letters

parts.note: cachet means prestige or distinction

explanation.surface: Suffering that comes from boundless distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' removes the first and last letters, C and T, from CACHET.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous dull pain, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Quality of lime green vegetable cut in Italy, cooked and passed round

indicators.note: passed round means the cooked letters are wrapped around the cut vegetable
cooked means the letters are reworked into a new order
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: kale is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: Some greens are chopped, cooked in Italy and handed round the table, with a hint of lime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is fodder: 'cooked' turns 'in Italy' into ALINITY, and 'passed round' wraps that around the trimmed vegetable after 'cut' drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime is a chemical base, so alkalinity is a property it has.

clue.text: Roman Catholic priest buried, bit of him dug up?

indicators.note: buried means the priest is put inside the other letters

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest is laid to rest, and later some part of him is unearthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried' places the priest inside the Catholic abbreviation. The definition is cryptic: a saint's bone dug up from a grave becomes an object of veneration.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a body part or belonging of a saint, kept and revered, often recovered from a grave.

clue.text: Gang pursued sort of lemur

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A gang went after some kind of lemur.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring-tailed lemur, with its banded tail, is the best-known species of lemur.

clue.text: Many touring capital almost miss the boat

indicators.note: touring means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a lot means many

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Seoul is the capital of South Korea

explanation.surface: A big group on a tour of a city nearly fails to catch their ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the capital's last letter, leaving SEOU, and 'touring' sends the word for many around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss the boat is an idiom for failing to take an opportunity, the same as losing out.

clue.text: Porter carries beheaded Egyptian leader in dish

indicators.note: carries means the first word holds the second inside

parts.note: Cole Porter was an American songwriter

indicators.note: beheaded means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Gamal Abdel Nasser was president of Egypt

explanation.surface: A porter carrying an Egyptian ruler's head on a platter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a baggage carrier but is the American songwriter; 'beheaded' leaves ASSER, and 'carries' puts that inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stew cooked slowly in the oven, and also the deep pot it is served in.

clue.text: See 11
Loud music acceptable

parts.note: f, forte, means loud in music
an air is a tune or piece of music

explanation.surface: Noisy music is perfectly all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means reasonable or acceptable, as in a fair result.

clue.text: US comedian Steven Wright's challenge when anyone seeks him moving with elevation, which is hardly possible

definitions.text: US comedian Steven Wright's challenge when anyone seeks him moving with elevation, which is hardly possible

parts.words: US comedian Steven Wright's challenge when anyone seeks him moving with elevation, which is hardly possible
parts.note: the one-liner by deadpan comic Steven Wright asks believers in mind over matter to lift his own limb by thought alone, a feat that is barely achievable

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a famous Steven Wright joke: he asks those who think objects can be moved by the mind to show it by lifting his arm, using only their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line is Steven Wright's joke, a mock call for telekinetic proof that no one can supply.

clue.text: See 11
Impudent rascal jokes about a king in prison

indicators.note: about means the jokes are placed around the other pieces

parts.note: japes are jokes or pranks

indicators.note: in means the king goes inside the prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A cheeky scoundrel makes jokes about a monarch behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the king inside the prison slang, the article comes before that, and 'about' wraps the jokes around the lot, splitting after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackanapes is an old word for a cheeky, impertinent person, especially a mischievous child.

clue.text: Wee Jan van MacDonald abandons one farm building

indicators.note: abandons means the following letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: a wee one is a small child, a bairn in Scots; with a Dutch first name and a Scottish surname, this child is a Dutch bairn
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Little Jan van MacDonald leaves one farm shed behind.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scottish word for a child; 'abandons' removes the I of 'one' from DUTCH BAIRN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is a farm building with a curved roof and open sides, used to store hay.

clue.text: Strong 24 with genteel ways in place of rest

indicators.note: in means the other pieces are put inside the place of rest

parts.note: a dorm (dormitory) is a place to sleep
U means upper class or genteel, as in the U and non-U usage debate
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way, so two ways give two of them

explanation.surface: Keeping a genteel manner while a gale blows through the dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways' is plural, so it gives ST twice. '24' points to the answer of 24-down, the first word of 24/21.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust storm is a strong gale carrying dust and sand across dry land.

clue.text: Musical beginning of counterpoint, romanticism

indicators.note: of means the answer is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A piece of music opens with counterpoint and a romantic mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words counterpoINT ROmanticism.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music, its short introduction.

clue.text: Plant has time in reserve

indicators.note: in means the time goes inside the reserve

parts.note: a sub, a substitute, is a reserve player
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a measure of time

explanation.surface: A plant has some time kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, so it is one kind of plant.

clue.text: See 11
Cows eating heartbroken girl

indicators.note: eating means the cows take the other letters inside them

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow

indicators.note: broken means the letters of heart are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some cows are eating while a girl's heart breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartbroken' is one word in the surface, but it splits: its first half is the fodder and 'broken' rearranges it to ATHER, which goes inside the old word for cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Katherine is a girl's name, so girl defines it by example.

clue.text: Picture puzzle with twisted ending, one upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the whole string is read bottom to top
twisted ending means the last two letters of the word swap round

parts.note: an enigma is a puzzle
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A picture puzzle with a twist at the end, viewed upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted ending' turns ENIGMA into ENIGAM; add I, and 'upside down' reverses ENIGAMI.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Bob and Benny who chased girls in grass

indicators.note: in means the comedian goes inside the other word

parts.note: to grass, or sing, is to inform on someone
Benny Hill, the British comic, was famous for sketches where he chased women round a park

explanation.surface: Bob and Benny go chasing girls through the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is old British slang for a shilling coin, worth twelve old pennies. Grass and sing are both British slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob was the everyday slang name for a shilling in pre-decimal British money.

clue.text: See 24
Utter magnitude of exasperated utterances

indicators.note: Utter means the word must be spoken, pointing to how it sounds

parts.note: size means magnitude

explanation.surface: Speak about the scale of someone's frustrated grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' seems to be an adjective meaning total, but it is a verb telling the solver to say SIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighs are long breaths let out in frustration, exactly what an exasperated person gives.

clue.text: See 11
Winch from Hurricane Agnes, you might say

parts.note: a hurricane is a gale, a violent rush of air
Agnes is a girl's name, so a young woman

explanation.surface: A lifting device bearing the name of a hurricane called Agnes.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurricanes are given names, often girls' names, so 'Hurricane Agnes' could be called a gale plus a young woman, as 'you might say' admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch with a horizontal drum used to haul ropes or raise anchors.

clue.text: As sovereign I should be off, gathering speed, stressing too much

indicators.note: gathering means the rearranged letters collect the speed unit inside them
should be off means the letters of the words are thrown out of order

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A king declares he ought to abdicate, and quickly, though he is laying it on thick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be off' rearranges 'As sovereign I' into OVEREASISING, and 'gathering' places the speed unit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overemphasise is to give too much stress or importance to something.

clue.text: West set about by going west, perhaps

indicators.note: set about means the actress's name is placed around the other letters

parts.note: Mae West was an American film star

indicators.note: going west in an across clue means the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: A western scene being set, with someone heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was a 1930s film star. 'going west' turns the little word round to YB, and 'set about' puts the actress around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe means perhaps: both express that something is possible.

clue.text: Add fertilizer to roots when dried out: end of life in three seconds

indicators.note: in means the other letters go inside the three seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so three seconds give three of them

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown into disorder
end of means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A gardener feeds the roots of dried-out plants, which die in moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges 'dried' to IDEDR, 'end of' takes the last letter of 'life', and 'in' puts the six letters inside the three seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: To side-dress is to put fertilizer along the sides of growing plants, where their roots reach.
